newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil seen cutting interest rates, credit - paper.
newsitem.headline: Brazil seen cutting interest rates, credit - paper.

text.p: Brazil's Central Bank is expected on Wednesday to continue lowering its basic interest rates as well as taking measures to restrict credit, the leading financial daily Gazeta Mercantil said.

The paper said the bank will lower its base interest rate (TBC) to either 1.54 percent or 1.56 percent, reduce its TBAN rate and adopt measures to rein in credit as a way of slowing growth in consumption, especially electronic goods and cars.
The bank's TBC rate was set at 1.58 percent and the TBAN rate at 1.78 percent for April, while the rate on interbank certificates of deposit (CDs) reached 1.66 percent, it said.

The government has pursued a contractionist monetary policy since April 1, when Hong Kong and Shanghai Bank (HKSB) brought into the country $930 million to buy private Brazilian bank Bamerindus, placing even more CDs in the market, it added.
